message.content:
Here are some of the most famous American composers—across a range of styles and eras—from the 19th century to today:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Modernist, “American” sound | *Appalachian Spring*, *Rodeo*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Broadway, symphonic | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *Symphonic Dances* |
| **John Williams** (b. 1942) | Film music | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (b. 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *The Hours* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | 20th‑century classical | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | “The First Black Composer” | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird* |
| **John Adams** (b. 1947) | Contemporary minimalism | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *The Unanswered Question* |
| **John Cage** (1912‑1992) | Avant‑garde | *4′33″*, *Sonatas and Interludes* |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (b. 1930) | Musical theatre | *Sweeney Todd*, *Into the Woods*, *Company* |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | March music | *The Stars and Stripes Forever*, *The Washington Post* |

These composers have had a lasting impact on American music, shaping everything from concert halls to Broadway stages and Hollywood soundtracks.
